name: Cogrunt
body:
Cogrunt
CR 3

This gray, squat creature resembles a bat-eared cross between an ape and a goblin. It wears a heavy, soot-stained apron and a bandolier full of tools and pouches.

XP 800
N Small fey
Init +3; Senses darkvision 120 ft., low-light vision; Perception +12

DEFENSE

AC 17, touch 14, flat-footed 14 (+3 Dex, +3 natural, +1 size)
hp 38 (7d6+14)
Fort +4, Ref +8, Will +7
DR 5/cold iron; SR 14

OFFENSE

Speed 30 ft.
Melee hand cannon +7 (1d6)
Ranged hand cannon +7 (1d6/x3)
Special Attacks disassemble (DC 15), speedy sabotage, tinker
Spell-Like Abilities (CL 7th; concentration +9)

At will—mending
1/day—make whole

STATISTICS

Str 10, Dex 17, Con 14, Int 15, Wis 14, Cha 15
Base Atk +3; CMB +2; CMD 15
Feats Deft Hands, Field Repair, Sabotage Specialist, Weapon Finesse
Skills Appraise +9, Craft (alchemy, firearms, mechanical) +12, Disable Device +20, Knowledge (engineering) +13, Perception +12, Stealth +17; Racial Modifiers +8 Disable Device, +4 Knowledge (engineering)
Languages Common, Gnome, Undercommon

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Disassemble (Ex)

As a standard action that does not provoke an attack of opportunity, a cogrunt can touch a non-magical object no more than one size category larger than itself, forcing either it or its wielder to attempt a DC 15 Reflex saving throw. On a failed save, the object is reduced to 1 hit point and gains the broken condition. Using this ability on an already broken object has no effect. The save DC is Intelligence-based.

Tinker (Ex)

Once per day, as a full-round action that provokes an attack of opportunity, a cogrunt can tinker with a construct, choosing to either repair it or tamper with it. A repaired construct regains 3d10 hit points. A construct that is tampered with must succeed at a DC 15 Fortitude save or be affected as if it failed a save against the sabotage construct spell at CL 7th. The save DC is Intelligence-based.

Speedy Sabotage (Ex)

When using the Disable Device skill, cogrunts treat all devices as being one category simpler for the purposes of determining how long it takes to use the skill. Thus, difficult devices count as tricky, tricky devices count as simple, and simple devices can be dismantled as a free action.

ECOLOGY

Environment any
Organization solitary, pair, or team (3–10)
Treasure standard (hand cannon, masterwork artisan tools, other treasure)

The great rivalry between bulabars and gremlins was fierce since times immemorial, the former loving to create technology and the latter to dismantle it. This hatred was redoubled when the first theories of an ancestral connection between those two types of fey were supposedly discovered by scholars. Still, it all pales to the affront to both bulabars and gremlins that the creation of cogrunts represented.

It is said that a powerful lord of the fey was taken by a fleeting interest in technology.

Unsure whose expertise would be best, he took representatives of both bulabars and gremlins and used powerful magic to meld them together, equipping his creation with a sturdy, humanoid body. Those creations, which he affectionately called cog runts, were supposed to be his assistants. Alas, an interest of a fey is a fleeting one, and he soon abandoned his interests for some other fancy. His creations, which proved able to breed true, were set free and across the planes they spread, journeying and tinkering, taking interest in many different crafts and professions, building and destroying with equal zeal, as long as a mechanical challenge was to be had. Seemingly undaunted by the hatred of their forebears or by the opinion of other, older fey more partial to nobility or whimsy, they found their calling in many different realms, planes and roles, under different skies and employers. Their name stuck and was very soon shortened to cogrunts, and to this day they bear it with great pride.

Cogrunts often serve as artisans or engineers, but are found just as often as apprentices and assistants to alchemists and wizards. They rarely have high ambitions, but love challenging themselves, and many become alchemists and investigators. Rogues are also common among cogrunts, as they carry a spark of mischief inherited from their gremlin ancestors, and their unmatched understanding of mechanisms allows them to easily crack open even the most complicated locks.

Finally, cogrunts adore firearms, but despite all their talent for creation, most lack the resources or skill to operate more complicated examples. They often create simple hand cannons, though more often use them as hammers than ranged weaponry.

Cogrunts are a welcome addition to armies that field constructs or siege weaponry, as they can maintain and repair such mechanisms with great proficiency. They are also capable combat engineers, rivaling dwarves in this profession, both fitting and seeing well in underground tunnels. Finally, cogrunts make incredible saboteurs, being able to dismantle, rig or otherwise tamper with different devices with blinding speed going as much by knowledge as by pure, almost supernatural instinct, allowing them to overcome even obstacles and mechanisms that they’ve never seen before.

An average cogrunt is just under 4 feet tall and weighs around 100 pounds.
